entities.summary:
Agnaptus was an ancient Greek architect who built the porch of Agnaptus at Olympia, a stoa that was considered one of the most impressive structures in the Altis. According to Pausanias, Agnaptus was the architect of the stoa, which was constructed during the 5th century BCE. The stoa was not only a notable architectural achievement but also a testament to the cultural and artistic achievements of ancient Greece. 

The construction of the stoa is believed to have occurred during the reign of the Elean king, Cleomenes II, who ruled Olympia from 307 to 259 BCE. The stoa was likely built as part of a larger complex that included the temple of Zeus, which was also a major architectural achievement of the time. 

The legacy of Agnaptus can be seen in the many architectural styles that were influenced by the stoa, including the use of Doric columns and the emphasis on proportion and balance. The stoa also played a significant role in the development of Western architecture, serving as a model for later buildings such as the Pantheon in Rome. 

In the 19th century, the stoa underwent a major restoration project, which aimed to return the building to its original form. The restoration was carried out by the German architect, Friedrich Schiller, who worked closely with the Greek authorities to recreate the stoa's original design. 

The porch of Agnaptus remains one of the most famous landmarks in Olympia, and its legacy continues to inspire architects and art historians to this day.
